display.title: Bubby Chaya Malka's Yiddish Stories, Part 1
display.summary_short: A grandmother tells her grandchildren Yiddish stories before Pesach: the Baal Shem Tov and the bear, Rashi's father's diamond, Dayeinu, the boy judge, Rabbi Meir and the lion, and the start of Shmuel HaNavi.
display.summary_long: First half of a home recording in which Bubby Chaya Malka tells her grandchildren stories in Yiddish, in the weeks before Pesach. She begins with the young Baal Shem Tov, who fears only Hashem and chases off a cruel man dressed as a bear so the cheder children can keep singing on their way to shul. Next, Rashi's poor father throws a precious diamond into the sea rather than let it decorate an idol, and an angel promises him a son who will light up the world with Torah. After a warm word to the grandchildren about being good and helping at home, she tells of a diamond found inside a big fish bought for Shabbos; of an old man who raises money for the poor for Pesach by promising to find the king's ring, which is found when the guests at his Seder sing 'Dayeinu'; and of a cheder boy whose game of 'trial' saves a falsely accused Jew. Then Rabbi Meir Baal HaNess keeps Shabbos alone in the desert and a lion guards him. The recording breaks off in the story of Chana and Shmuel HaNavi, which continues in Part 2.
display.lesson: Trust Hashem and fear nothing else; honor Shabbos and Yom Tov, help the poor, and be good children who make their parents happy.

advisories.note: A Jew is falsely accused and jailed, and a mob comes to the trial with axes and torches ready to attack the Jews; a wicked minister urges harsh decrees.
A man dressed as a bear frightens children and is beaten off; Rabbi Meir is left alone in a desert where a lion approaches him.
Poor families with nothing for Yom Tov; a man loses all his money.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov and the bear
segments.summary: The young Baal Shem Tov, who fears only Hashem, drives off a cruel man dressed as a bear so the cheder children can keep singing on the way to shul.

segments.title: Rashi's father and the diamond
segments.summary: Rashi's poor father throws a precious diamond into the sea rather than sell it to decorate an idol, and is promised a son who will light up the world with Torah.

segments.title: Be good children
segments.summary: The grandmother tells the children that obeying parents and helping at home makes the family happy, praising each grandchild.

segments.title: The diamond in the fish
segments.summary: A rich man hides his fortune in a diamond in his hat; a fish swallows it, and Yosef, who always buys the best fish for Shabbos, finds it.

segments.title: Dayeinu: the old man and the king's ring
segments.summary: An old man who provides Pesach for the poor promises to find the king's lost ring; at his Seder the king hears 'Dayeinu' and finds the thief.

segments.title: The butcher, the storekeeper and the boy judge
segments.summary: A Jewish storekeeper is falsely accused of theft, and a cheder boy's test with hot water proves the truth.

segments.title: Rabbi Meir Baal HaNess and the lion
segments.summary: Left alone in the desert because he will not travel on Shabbos, Rabbi Meir is guarded by a lion that carries him back to the caravan.

segments.title: Chana and Shmuel HaNavi (beginning)
segments.summary: Chana prays for a child, Eli HaKohen blesses her, and she brings little Shmuel to the Beis HaMikdash; the story continues in Part 2.
